behavior can be defended.

the five model tables and save a PBIX.

1. Why this lesson matters
A Power BI report can look correct while its preparation/model is wrong. This lesson builds one
trust layer so later DAX/reporting is based on data whose grain, relationships and refresh
behavior can be defended.
2. What you are learning
Prepare the fact/dimensions with justified Power Query steps while preserving raw data and
documenting every row-count change.
3. What you already need / prerequisite

Raw value -> justified transformation -> explicit data type -> quality check -> prepared value.
Every row-count change gets a reason.

Data type = how a value is interpreted, such as text/date/whole/decimal. Exact duplicate =
identical row at the stated grain. Business validity = value obeys business rule; type validity

PBM2 - Follow with me once
7. Follow with me once - fully worked teacher demonstration
A safe transformation is repeatable, justified and testable. Trim formatting noise, standardize
only confirmed equivalent values, set business-appropriate types, remove an exact duplicate
only after proving it is exact at the stated grain, and keep unresolved unmatched/invalid values
visible. Type validity and business validity are different: 1.20 is numeric but may violate a
0%-100% discount rule. Teacher action: Use the practice workbook and complete P-PBM2: Clean
a fresh fact query containing one exact duplicate, one invalid date, one 130% discount and one
unknown product key.
8. What you should see / be able to say
Every row-count change is explained; invalid/unmatched values remain visible; no raw-sheet
manual edit is required.
9. Why it worked
The action preserves source evidence, makes grain/model assumptions explicit and creates a
testable checkpoint. Power BI output is trusted only when independent
row/key/total/filter/refresh controls agree.
10. Common beginner mistakes
Replacing all errors with zero/blank; deleting rows without a reason; changing raw Excel source
manually; removing a duplicate before proving exact equality at the intended grain; hiding
unknown keys.
11. If you get stuck - recovery ladder
If a type change creates errors, inspect the original values and isolate the failure instead of
replacing all errors with zero/blank. If row count changed unexpectedly, step backward through
Applied Steps until the count changes. 1) Restate grain/goal. 2) Identify the exact Power BI area
or query. 3) Reveal only the next structural action. 4) Open matching protected review only after
a saved attempt. 5) Close review and solve a changed retry.

one unknown product key. Keep a before/after row-count note and a quality log.

manual edit is required.

A Power BI report can look correct while its preparation/model is wrong. This lesson builds one

PBM3 - Follow with me once
7. Follow with me once - fully worked teacher demonstration
A fact table records events/measurements at a consistent grain and usually has many rows.
Dimensions describe entities used to group/filter and require a unique key on the one side. A star
schema keeps the fact in the center with Product/Customer/Region/Date-like dimensions around
it. Model clarity begins with one sentence describing the grain of every table. Teacher action:
Use the practice workbook and complete P-PBM3: Given Orders, Products, Stores and Calendar,
state the grain of each, choose fact/dimensions and prove the intended one-side keys are unique
before drawing the star.
8. What you should see / be able to say
Every table has a written grain; intended one-side keys are unique; fact is central in a
recognizable star.
9. Why it worked
The action preserves source evidence, makes grain/model assumptions explicit and creates a
testable checkpoint. Power BI output is trusted only when independent
row/key/total/filter/refresh controls agree.
10. Common beginner mistakes
Calling every lookup-like table a dimension without checking key uniqueness; building
relationships before grain statements; forcing many-to-many because the one side is dirty;
mixing fact/dimension responsibilities.
11. If you get stuck - recovery ladder
If the dimension key is not unique, do not create many-to-many as a shortcut. Identify whether
whitespace, duplicate business entities or wrong grain caused the duplicate. 1) Restate
grain/goal. 2) Identify the exact Power BI area or query. 3) Reveal only the next structural action.
4) Open matching protected review only after a saved attempt. 5) Close review and solve a
changed retry.

7. Follow with me once - fully worked teacher demonstration
Relationships encode business logic. A one-to-many relationship requires uniqueness on the
intended one side; unmatched foreign keys on the fact side are a different issue. Default to
single-direction filtering from dimension to fact. If Power BI refuses 1:*, investigate
duplicate/blank/type-mismatched one-side keys instead of switching to many-to-many to make
the warning disappear. Teacher action: Use the practice workbook and complete P-PBM4: On a
changed model, create Product/Store/Date 1:* relationships to Orders and prove single-direction
filter propagation with a temporary count/sum visual.

matching fact rows.

testable checkpoint. Power BI output is trusted only when independent
row/key/total/filter/refresh controls agree.
10. Common beginner mistakes
Using bidirectional filtering to make a visual 'work'; ignoring duplicate/blank/type-mismatched
one-side keys; confusing unmatched fact keys with duplicate dimension keys; trusting
relationships without a filter test.

propagate, verify active relationship, direction and matching key values before enabling
bidirectional filtering. 1) Restate grain/goal. 2) Identify the exact Power BI area or query. 3)

attempt. 5) Close review and solve a changed retry.

Model validation and trust checks
Practice: matching PBM block in C1_M05_POWERBI_MODELING_PRACTICE_GUIDE_RC1.pdf
1. Why this lesson matters
A Power BI report can look correct while its preparation/model is wrong. This lesson builds one
trust layer so later DAX/reporting is based on data whose grain, relationships and refresh
behavior can be defended.
2. What you are learning
Produce a validation log that proves the model did not silently lose/duplicate data and records
unresolved quality issues.
3. What you already need / prerequisite
Prerequisite: PBM5. The new interface/model concept is still explained from first principles.
4. Picture it in your head
Trust = row reconciliation + key checks + unmatched-key checks + type/business checks +
control total + filter-path proof.
5. New words before we use them
Reconciliation = independent agreement between source/prepared/model controls. Invariant =
value/count expected not to change without reason. Filter-propagation test = prove dimension
filter reaches intended fact rows. Unresolved issue = known quality risk kept visible.
6. Watch / visual source
RECOMMENDED_VISUAL. Chandoo - Data Modelling & Star Schema for Power BI | 00:43-18:07.
Why use it: Revisit the complete modeling flow while building an independent trust/validation
log. Internal fallback: PBM6 learner book + guide contain the seven-control validation contract.
Open primary/reference
PBM6 - Follow with me once
7. Follow with me once - fully worked teacher demonstration
A model is trustworthy only when multiple independent checks agree. Reconcile source/prepared
row counts, fact-grain uniqueness, dimension-key uniqueness, unmatched foreign keys,
